questions.prompt: Your call to the payment gateway times out after 30 seconds. What do you do before retrying?

options.text: Retry straight away; a timeout means the charge failed
Ask the gateway for the payment status, then retry with the same idempotency key if needed
Show the customer an error and ask them to pay again
Raise the timeout to 60 seconds so it doesn't happen again

questions.strong_answer: A timeout means the outcome is unknown. Check the payment status first, and only retry with the same idempotency key so the gateway can't charge twice.

questions.prompt: The payment webhook arrives before your API has saved the payment response. The order still says 'created'. What should the handler do?

options.text: Reject the webhook; it arrived out of order
Wait a few seconds and check again
Move the order forward to 'captured' with a conditional update, and ignore later events that would move it back
Store the webhook and process it in a nightly batch

questions.strong_answer: Treat the order as a state machine that only moves forward. Whichever signal arrives first applies a conditional update; the other becomes a no-op.

questions.prompt: One downstream service gets slow (not down), and soon every endpoint of your API is timing out. What's the most likely cause?

options.text: Slow calls are holding threads or connections from a shared pool, so healthy endpoints queue behind them
The downstream service is sending bad data
The load balancer is misconfigured
Your servers need more CPU

questions.strong_answer: Slow is worse than down. Waiting calls exhaust a shared pool. Timeouts on every call, separate pools per dependency and a circuit breaker stop the spread.

questions.prompt: Three layers of your stack each retry failed calls 3 times. A dependency starts failing. What happens?

options.text: Each user request gets up to 3 extra tries, which helps it recover
One request can become up to 64 calls, piling load onto a service that's already struggling
Retries smooth out the failures over time
Nothing; retries only fire on network errors

questions.strong_answer: Retries multiply across layers: 4 attempts at each of 3 layers is 64 calls. Retry at one layer, with backoff and jitter, and cap retries with a budget.

questions.prompt: Two users book the last seat at the same moment, and both bookings succeed. Your code checks the seat is free before booking. What's the fix?

options.text: Check twice before booking
Put a mutex around the booking code in the app
Let the database decide: a conditional update or a unique constraint, then check the result
Add a short sleep so requests don't overlap

questions.strong_answer: Check-then-act is the race. Make the write itself conditional, or rely on a unique constraint, so only one booking can succeed.

questions.prompt: A quick ALTER TABLE on orders caused a checkout outage, even though it should take milliseconds. Why?

options.text: It waited for a lock behind a long-running transaction, and every new query queued behind it
The database ran out of disk space
Migrations should only run at night
The ORM generated a slow query

questions.strong_answer: Even a fast ALTER needs a strong lock. If it waits behind a long transaction, all new queries queue behind it. Set a lock timeout and roll schema changes out in steps.

questions.prompt: A popular cache key expires, and database load spikes for about a minute. What do you check first?

options.text: Whether lots of requests missed the cache at the same moment and all hit the database
Whether the database needs a bigger instance
Whether the expiry time is too short, so you can make it longer
Whether the cache server restarted

questions.strong_answer: Check for a stampede first: many requests missing the same key at once. Fix it with request coalescing, jittered expiry or an early refresh.

questions.prompt: After a price change, some users see the old price for far longer than the 5-minute cache TTL. What's the best explanation?

options.text: The TTL setting isn't being applied
Users' browsers are slow
Another cache layer is serving it, or a slow reader wrote the old value back after the update
The database update failed

questions.strong_answer: Look for other layers (CDN, in-process caches, replicas) and the stale write-back race. Versioning cached values stops old writes from winning.
